title: INVESTIGATOR theme (V2)
description: A theme for INVESTIGATOR, for the custom themes folder or `CONFIG.Investigator.installTheme`.

$schema.description: The schema for this file, so an editor can check it: ignored by INVESTIGATOR.

fonts.description: The theme's type: its typefaces, and the size of body text.

layout.description: How the character sheets are laid out. `"standard"` (the default) has Foundry's titlebar over the sheet. `"full-frame"` runs the sheet up to the window's top edge, under a see-through titlebar: a strip across the top, still the titlebar (it drags the window, and a double click on it minimizes it), with its buttons in a row at the right, a faint tint on hover, and no title. The logo runs up under it, but its text keeps below it, scaled down to fit. The portrait and the sidebar move to the left. The title shows only when the window is minimized. Windows without a logo (items, say) keep the standard titlebar. The titlebar's look is the `appFrame` recipe's `layout: full-frame` variant.

globalCss.description: Raw CSS, in the themed root, unscoped: an escape hatch for what the catalogue can't express (and for loading a folder theme's fonts). Not supported: it can break as the markup changes.

polarity.description: Whether the theme is light or dark. Sets `color-scheme`.

wallpaper.description: The colour the sheet's backdrop averages to, shown while images load.

surfaceNested.description: What content inside content sits on.

control.description: The fill of controls: buttons, toggle tracks.

text.description: The default ink. Legible on `surface`, `surfaceNested` and `control`.

line.description: Structural lines: control outlines, separators, heading rules.

feedback.description: The colour of hover, focus and drag-over feedback.

danger.description: Something bad or destructive. Legible as text on surfaces.

warning.description: Something that needs attention, less serious than `danger`.

surfaceSolid.description: `surface` for things that overlap or scroll over other content (menus, sticky headers, cards). Only a theme whose `surface` is translucent needs to set it, to an opaque colour. Default: `surface`.

textMuted.description: Ink for secondary information. Default: `text`, faded towards `surfaceSolid`.

link.description: Ink for links within prose. Default: `accent`.

onAccent.description: Ink on an `accent` fill. Default: black or white, by contrast.

onDanger.description: Ink on a `danger` fill. Default: black or white, by contrast.

onWarning.description: Ink on a `warning` fill. Default: black or white, by contrast.

onSuccess.description: Ink on a `success` fill. Default: black or white, by contrast.

onInfo.description: Ink on an `info` fill. Default: black or white, by contrast.

radius.description: The corner radius of boxes and controls. Default: `0.25em`.

elevation.description: The shadow of anything floating. Default: `0 0 0.5em black`.

cardGap.description: The spacing between cards, as a CSS `gap` value (a row gap, then a column gap, or one for both), and around a card array. Default: `0.5em`.

ThemePalette.description: A theme's palette: the values the catalogue is built from, each with one meaning (docs/theming.md, "Palette"). The core is required; the rest is worked out from it unless the theme sets it.

baseSize.description: The size of the sheet's body text, which everything else is relative to, e.g. `"16px"`. Default: `1em` (the window's).

body.description: The `body` text style: prose and controls.

display.description: The `display` text style: titles, headings, tabs, labels, buttons.

scale.description: A correction for how big the typeface looks, multiplying every size the style is set at: a face that looks small at a given size (a condensed one, small caps) wants more than 1. Not a size: the catalogue says how big each kind of text is. Default: `1`.

ThemeFont.description: A text style's typeface, and how it's set. Every field is optional: what's left out is the window's for `body`, and `body`'s for `display` (except `scale`).

ThemeCatalogue.description: A theme's overrides of the catalogue's recipes, by recipe name, and of the state layers everywhere in the theme (`states`), which they **patch**: `&` is anything in that state. A state's default can't be beaten from a recipe's `base` or `variants` (the states come after them), only here, or in a recipe's own `states`. The element states (pressed, disabled...) are only a recipe's, not the theme's.

ThemeStyle.description:
A style in a theme's override: CSS properties in camelCase (a number is pixels, for properties that take a length; an array is fallbacks), custom properties, and nested rules keyed by a selector that contains `&` (`&:hover`, `&[data-selected]`) or an at-rule (`@media ...`), as in CSS nesting.

Values are CSS. A palette entry is its custom property (`PaletteVar`): `color: "var(--inv-accent)"`.
